name: Secondary Central Precocious Puberty in Female
aliases: Acquired Central Precocious Puberty in Girls

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Criteria for Central Precocious Puberty

criteria.description: Onset of breast development before 8 years of age
Elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) response to GnRH stimulation test consistent with pubertal activation
Bone age advanced by more than 1 year compared to chronological age
Identification of an underlying CNS lesion or condition triggering puberty

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early thelarche before age 8, pubertal LH response on GnRH stimulation, and evidence of an underlying CNS cause
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires differentiation from idiopathic CPP and peripheral precocious puberty.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Advanced bone age relative to chronological age

common.symptomName: Mood changes related to hormonal fluctuations

occasional.symptomName: Visual disturbances from hypothalamic or pituitary mass effect
searchTerms: blurred or double vision due to pituitary tumor

occasional.symptomName: Nausea or vomiting related to intracranial pressure
searchTerms: upset stomach linked to brain swelling

laboratory: Elevated basal and GnRH-stimulated luteinizing hormone (LH) levels
Increased estradiol levels consistent with pubertal status
Normal or elevated follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) with pubertal pattern
imaging: MRI of hypothalamic-pituitary region showing CNS lesions (e.g., hamartomas, tumors, cysts)
Advanced bone age on hand/wrist radiograph
genetic: Possible mutations in MKRN3 gene in idiopathic cases (less common in secondary CPP)
No specific genetic markers for secondary CPP; genetic testing to exclude other causes
other: Growth velocity acceleration documented by serial height measurements
Neuroendocrine evaluation to exclude peripheral precocious puberty

distinguishingFeatures: No identifiable CNS lesion on MRI
More common in females without secondary causes
GnRH stimulation test shows prepubertal LH response
Elevated sex steroids independent of hypothalamic-pituitary axis
May be caused by ovarian cysts, adrenal tumors, or exogenous hormones

redFlags: Rapid neurological deterioration or new neurological deficits
Severe headache with vomiting indicating increased intracranial pressure
Visual field loss or sudden visual changes
references: Carel JC, Léger J. Precocious puberty. N Engl J Med. 2008;358(22):2366-2377.
